title: TEACHERS’ AND STUDENTS’ PERCEPTIONS TOWARDS THE USE OF CHATGPT TO IMPROVE WRITING IN THE MALAYSIAN SECONDARY SCHOOL CONTEXT
extended_summary:
This paper examines how Malaysian secondary school students and English teachers perceive the use of ChatGPT for improving students’ English writing. The study is motivated by growing interest in generative AI in education and the relative lack of evidence focused on secondary school settings, especially compared with the larger literature in higher education. The authors specifically investigate perceived effectiveness, how ChatGPT is used for writing-related purposes, and what factors shape adoption.

The approach studied is the use of ChatGPT as a writing support tool rather than a formally implemented experimental intervention. Participants described using ChatGPT for drafting essays, revising text, grammar checking, vocabulary development, proofreading, idea generation, and obtaining feedback. Teachers also reported using ChatGPT to create more personalized lesson materials and, in at least one example, assigning homework in which students used ChatGPT to write an essay and then discussed feedback and revisions in class.

The study used a qualitative design with open-ended online questionnaires. The sample included 20 respondents from six public secondary schools in Sabah, Malaysia: 12 students and 8 English teachers. Students were described as having varied English proficiency levels and differing prior exposure to ChatGPT. Data were thematically analyzed to identify common perceptions, reported uses, and adoption factors.

The main conclusion is that both students and teachers generally viewed ChatGPT positively as a helpful aid for English writing, especially because it can provide fast, personalized feedback and support tasks such as proofreading and idea generation. At the same time, participants identified important challenges, including limited access to devices or internet, uneven digital literacy, and concerns about overreliance on AI that could undermine independent writing development. The authors conclude that AI integration in writing instruction has promise, but should be balanced with conventional teaching and supported by attention to infrastructure and teacher support.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed qualitative study with a clear methodology, sample, and thematic analysis, but it does not use experimental or quasi-experimental designs and provides only self-reported perceptions rather than direct outcome measures.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially beneficial but unclear impact on secondary students’ writing and teacher efficiency because findings are based on perceptions only, with no causal design, standardized outcome data, or effect sizes.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used by Malaysian secondary school students and English teachers to support English writing through drafting, revising, proofreading, grammar correction, vocabulary expansion, idea generation, and creating sample texts or lesson materials.

ChatGPT used conversationally to provide personalized feedback and suggestions on students’ writing, including asking how to improve original work and discussing AI-generated feedback in subsequent class sessions.

finding.finding_summary: Across 20 participants (12 students, 8 teachers) from six Malaysian secondary schools, respondents generally perceived ChatGPT as effective for improving English writing, especially grammar, vocabulary, idea generation, drafting, revision, and overall writing quality. Evidence is based on qualitative self-reports rather than direct pre/post writing assessments, and no effect sizes or confidence intervals were reported.
finding.measure: Open-ended questionnaire responses about perceived improvement in English writing proficiency and writing-related uses of ChatGPT

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported that ChatGPT saved time in writing and teaching-related tasks by offering rapid feedback, grammar checking, and quick generation of example texts or personalized lesson materials. These efficiency benefits were described qualitatively by students and teachers, with no quantified time-saved metric reported.
finding.measure: Self-reported perceptions of time savings, convenience, and usefulness for teaching/material preparation

finding.finding_summary: Some teachers perceived ChatGPT as encouraging critical thinking because students must formulate questions or prompts to obtain useful answers, but participants also expressed concern that overreliance could undermine students’ ability to write independently. These findings are perception-based and not supported by direct performance measures of critical thinking or independent writing transfer.
finding.measure: Open-ended questionnaire responses on critical thinking, independence, and overreliance concerns
